root_cause.text: The AMD IOMMU debugfs MMIO offset validation in `iommu_mmio_write()` used a 4-byte boundary check even though `iommu_mmio_show()` performs an 8-byte `readq()` access, allowing an offset near `mmio_phys_end` to pass validation and trigger an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description says the check `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4` “assumes a 4-byte access,” while `iommu_mmio_show()` “uses readq() to perform an 8-byte (64-bit) read”; the patch changes the check to `iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64)`, confirming the mismatch between validated range and actual access size.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE description says the check `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4` “assumes a 4-byte access,” while `iommu_mmio_show()` “uses readq() to perform an 8-byte (64-bit) read”; the patch changes the check to `iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64)`, confirming the mismatch between validated range and actual access size.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the MMIO bounds check to use the correct 64-bit access size when validating the write offset.
intent_record.what: The bounds check in `iommu_mmio_write()` was changed from comparing `iommu->dbg_mmio_offset` against `iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4` to comparing it against `iommu->mmio_phys_end - sizeof(u64)`, while keeping the same error handling (`set dbg_mmio_offset to -1` and return `-EINVAL`).
intent_record.how: This changes the validation threshold for MMIO writes so the code now enforces enough remaining space for a 64-bit value instead of a fixed 4-byte amount. As a result, oversized or out-of-range writes are rejected correctly for 8-byte accesses, preventing invalid MMIO access near the end of the mapped region.

grouping_result.intent: Fix the MMIO bounds check to use the correct 64-bit access size when validating the write offset.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly matches the root cause: it fixes the MMIO offset validation to account for the 64-bit access size, which is the issue that allowed an out-of-bounds read near mmio_phys_end.

candidates.rationale: This bounds check uses a 4-byte limit even though the MMIO access is an 8-byte read in iommu_mmio_show(), allowing offsets near the end of the region to pass validation and later cause an out-of-bounds read.

vuln_statements.explanation: This validation uses a 4-byte boundary even though the debugfs MMIO read path performs an 8-byte readq() access, so an offset near mmio_phys_end can incorrectly pass and lead to an out-of-bounds read.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function contains the vulnerable validation logic and the out-of-bounds condition is visible directly. In `iommu_mmio_write()`, the offset check is `if (iommu->dbg_mmio_offset > iommu->mmio_phys_end - 4)`, but `iommu_mmio_show()` later does `value = readq(iommu->mmio_base + iommu->dbg_mmio_offset);`, which is an 8-byte access. This means an offset that is valid for a 4-byte boundary can still cause `readq()` to read past `mmio_phys_end`. The snippet does not show any corrected 8-byte bound check, so the fix is not present.
